summary: This study investigates the structural characteristics and annealing effects of ZnO epitaxial films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on c-plane sapphire substrates. The films are predominantly c-plane oriented with a minor (1011) orientation, which is reduced upon thermal annealing. The ALD process uses DEZn and H2O as precursors, and the films show significant structural improvement after annealing, with intrinsic basal plane stacking faults becoming the dominant structural defects.
evidence: The text states that the ALD method was used to fabricate ZnO epi-films on c-plane sapphire. The main precursors were Diethylzinc (DEZn) and H2O. The process temperature was maintained at 200 /C176 C during deposition, and thermal annealing was performed at temperatures ranging from 300 to 800 /C176 C. The study reports that the structural characteristics of the ZnO films were significantly improved upon thermal annealing, with intrinsic basal plane stacking faults being the predominant structural defects.
